claim: Folding a commander's standing fronts (and empty-land columns) into one Transit drops the other columns' surges; the join and empty-land merge are not gated on rules 21.
evidence: The surge belongs to the land being taken: Session.set_surge writes the same surge_to onto every packet bound for that land and sheet.surges is keyed by destination, so two columns into one land cannot order different surges from the UI or the AI. test_v21 _surge_together: two fronts take The Gate and push on to Quarry with its one surge on 20 of 20 seeds, before and after the change. The join and the empty-land merge were behaviourally no-ops for rules <= 20 (columns already merged), but not literally the old path. Resolution: fixed: both gated on map.rules >= 21 (rules <= 20 take the old code path), and the joined side's order is built by _merge_same_owner (all its lands; its surge only if the columns agree, as rules 20 did for a crafted sheet); surge test pinned

claim: The battle train (counts=false) is never toppled when its army is destroyed.
evidence: Diorama._cull's share == 0 branch topples every non-counting figure of the group (officer, drummer, colours, and now the train), and set_count calls _cull for every group. Probe v21 fights a 38 v 33 battle to the end: the loser has 0 figures standing, horse and guns included. Resolution: no change; v21 now states the fact.

claim: A region won and lost again in the same report keeps flaring in the old holder's colours until REGION_FX expires.
evidence: refresh() set _region_fx only when a new holder appeared and never cleared it when the set broke; region_won() stayed >= 0. Resolution: fixed: refresh erases a region's moment when its holder is no longer that owner; v202 fact: lost again before its moment is over, the flare ends with it

claim: Under rules 21, _settle_arrows treats every order of the clash's commanders into the land as the clash column: the second column's arrow is dropped, and the first may carry the clash's survivor count.
evidence: _settle_arrows matched owner and destination only, which was right while the engine merged a commander's columns. Probe v21 _clash_spares_the_other (Ridge and Harbor on The Gate, Varek out on Ridge): Harbor's arrow showed 6 (the clash's survivors) with the old matching, 7 (its own) with the fix; watched failing, then passing. Resolution: under rules 21 only the order on the clash's own border (from/to) is settled.

claim: A one-sided or split surge is dropped when a commander's fronts join (or walk in together).
evidence: A surge belongs to the land being taken: Session.set_surge and set_attack put the land's one surge on every column bound there, and the AI (ai.gd packets()) gives every column of one attack the attack's surge. Only the random test bot (bot.gd) can make columns into one land disagree, and then rules 21 does exactly what rules 20's merge always did (no surge). Pinned by test_v21 _surge_together (both fronts push on with the land's surge, 20 of 20 seeds).

claim: _lift never animates or hides the figure: _place has no lift arm.
evidence: Diorama._place has had a "lift" arm since v2.0 (up and away over 0.45 s, then node.visible = false), and _process advances t for every figure. v203 now asserts the lifted figure's node is hidden: passes.

claim: Rules 20 merged melee fronts have no fromIds, so the second column's fate mark is skipped.
evidence: The melee event has written fromIds (Array(_froms(t))) on every front since before this change (git show HEAD:engine/resolve.gd line 849), so a rules 20 merged front lists both lands and either ghost matches it.

claim: The battle swoop's tween isn't tracked, so a skip mid-swoop leaves the view in the battle frame; stand_back's is_valid() is true for a finished tween.
evidence: The swoop tween was untracked: restore_view couldn't stop it. The is_valid half is wrong (a finished Godot tween is invalid). Resolution: swoop_to keeps its tween in _swoop_tw and restore_view kills it (only a skip, whose battle is aborted, stops a swoop). v202 _skip_mid_swoop: skipped at zoom 1.22, back at the fit 0.44.

claim: The train is toppled when its host group is wiped while the army fights on; the docs say it falls only with the army.
evidence: _cull's share == 0 branch toppled every non-counting figure of the group, the train included. Resolution: the train is skipped there unless the army's count is 0, and when the army's count reaches 0 every piece of its train falls, whichever group it stood with; v21's big battle still ends with the loser at 0 pieces standing.

claim: Under rules 21, a column whose front fell back or was destroyed is marked as taking the land when another front of the same commander took it.
evidence: ghosts() decided TOOK from who holds the land before looking at the column's own front. test_v21 _fate_of_a_broken_front (Ridge's front of 2 destroyed, Harbor's 15 take The Gate, 51 seeds) fails with the check switched off and passes with it. Resolution: under rules 21 a TOOK column is checked against its own melee front (_own_front): fell back or destroyed, it says so.

claim: Under rules < 21 (old saves) the clash picture uses one order's strength, not the merged army that fought it.
evidence: _clash_side preferred the board's order and _settle_arrows overwrote the event's sizes with the order's. Resolution: the clash is told with the event's sizes (the army that fought it) in both rules; probe v202 _old_rules_clash: a rules 20 game's clash shows 18 on the map, matching the event.

claim: A hidden settings panel swallows Esc in _input, so the pause menu no longer opens.
evidence: main.gd creates the settings panel when it opens and queue_frees it on closed, so it is never in the tree hidden. Hardened anyway: Esc is taken only while the panel is visible in the tree.

claim: In a rules 20 save, a clash told with the merged army's count leaves the commander's other column into the land drawn as well: the map shows the army and its part (18 and 9).
evidence: clash_hides hid only the clash's own road; RV-003 F2 made the road carry the merged 18. Presentation only (rules 20 replay untouched). Resolution: under rules < 21 (clash_sides' merged flag) every order of a clash commander bound for the other's land stands aside while the clash is told. Probe v202 _old_rules_clash: both columns stand aside, the map shows 18.

claim: A melee of mixed commanders, one on two fronts, is titled with one army per front ("3 armies storm it at once").
evidence: The subtitle counted fronts. Resolution: it counts commanders, and names the sides when there are more fronts than commanders. Probe v21 _mixed_melee (Dad from Ridge and Harbor, Ysolde from Docks): "2 armies storm it from three sides at once", one more face (Ysolde's) and Dad's second front by its land.

claim: A free-for-all's dice pairs are not laid out in field order (only a melee's are), though the goal says melee or free-for-all; tags then point elsewhere.
evidence: _in_field_order returned early unless _melee (battle_theater.gd:1109). The ordering gap is real; the 'tags point elsewhere' part is not: each tag is placed over its own pair (front_marks.gd place). Blind verifier: partial, same reasons.

claim: In a melee with several Fortune calls, a call's narration names commanders owed for another call (it reads the battle-wide rebate).
evidence: _show_call read _event()['rebate'] (the battle's sum) and only excluded the spender; with Varek's and Dad's calls in one melee of three, Dad's call named Hask. Fixed: each Fortune call carries its own 'owed' (resolve.gd, both paths), the line reads it, and a live call is looked up in the re-resolved event (_owed_by). test_v22 _each_call_its_own (31 seeds) fails without it. Blind verifier: confirmed.

claim: A casualty can fall before any musket ball arrives: the fall time is estimated from the group centre and an undelayed shot, not the shots actually fired.
evidence: _shot_at = clock + 0.22 + flight(centre) while each man fires at 0.18 + r (r up to 0.16) and his ball flies to a jittered mark; a volley of one to three men could fall up to ~0.06 s early. Real but small. Fixed: _shot_at is the earliest real arrival (FIRE_AT - t + flight per man). Probe v22: 8 volleys timed, 0 early. Blind verifier: partial (overstated).

claim: The Fortune line names everyone in the battle's combined rebate, not the victims of this throw-away (found independently of codex F4).
evidence: Same defect as codex F4, found independently by the other reviewer on the same packet. Fixed with codex F4.
